A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 36-page versions of the same paper, including Appendices A–G. Text extraction and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content; differences concern acknowledgments, version metadata and reference-page layout.

before.justification: v3 reports original exploitability and head-to-head evaluations from 7,000 training runs in Section 5, with additional runtime, tabular-solver and sensitivity results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original 7,000-run empirical comparison in Section 5 and the original runtime, solver, validation and sensitivity results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The exploitability computation in Section 4 and Appendix A and the algorithm adaptations in Section 5.1 and Appendix C are unchanged, including the reverse-KL modification of PPO used for MMD.

E1.justification: Both use the same five principal games: LD2D5F, DH3, ADH3, PTTT and APTTT. The Leduc validation and smaller Liar’s Dice runtime benchmarks in Appendices A and D are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Section 5.1 retains NFSP, PSRO, ESCHER, R-NaD, PPO, PPG and MMD. Comparator membership within the head-to-head, tabular-solver, runtime and implementation-validation comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix G retain the same 10-million-step budgets, 50 tuning configurations, selection of five configurations for evaluation, three-layer 512-unit networks, metrics and testing procedures. Appendix experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B and D–F retain the same Dark Hex strategy analysis, implementation validation, entropy sensitivity, hyperparameter-importance analysis and wider PSRO oracle-training sweep. No analysis is added, removed or revised.

E5.justification: Both report three seeds per tuning configuration and ten fresh seeds per evaluation configuration. The appendix seed counts, boxplots, interquartile bands and standard-deviation reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported values, curves and findings match throughout, including Figures 2–3, runtime and solver results in Tables 2–3, and the supplementary results in Appendix F and Table 7. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The game and exploitability definitions in Section 2, Equation 1, sequence-form reasoning in Appendix A and deterministic Dark Hex winning-strategy argument in Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same policy-gradient hypothesis, five-game exploitability contribution and finding that the evaluated FP-, DO- and CFR-based approaches fail to outperform generic policy-gradient methods.

C2.justification: Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning game diversity, algorithm variants, hyperparameter search and training duration. The regularization and entropy-based explanations in Section 3 and Appendix E are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Code links and their destinations, implementation descriptions, hyperparameter defaults, hardware specifications and runtime/memory information are unchanged, including Appendices A, C, F and G.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The bibliography contains identical entries after accounting for whitespace and page breaks; no references were added or removed.

P1.justification: Section 8 adds acknowledgment of NSF CCF-2443068, an AI2050 Early Career Fellowship and NSERC PSG-D Fellowship 599271-2025. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment and reference pages have minor spacing and page-break changes on pages 10–15. Figures 1–15, Tables 1–7 and all appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 provides fuller funding acknowledgment in Section 8 and minor version and layout updates. The methods, empirical evidence, theoretical arguments, limitations and reproducibility information remain identical, establishing no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
